title: Can four-sided skyline reporting match ordinary range reporting?
formal: Preprocess a static set $P\subseteq[N]^2$ of $N$ points, with distinct coordinates in each dimension, on a word RAM with $\Theta(\log N)$-bit words. Is there a structure using $N\log^{O(1)}N$ words that reports the skyline of $P\cap([a,b]\times[c,d])$ in worst-case $O(\log\log N+k)$ time, where $k$ is the number of reported points? A point is on the skyline if no other point in the query rectangle is at least as large in both coordinates and strictly larger in one.
context:
Think of records scored on two attributes, with larger values preferred. A range filter first selects the eligible records; the skyline then removes options that are worse on both attributes. For points (1,5), (3,3), (4,4), and (5,1), the full-set skyline excludes (3,3). A rectangle that includes (3,3) but cuts off (4,4) can make it a skyline point. Therefore, storing only the global skyline loses information needed for later queries.

The output can be much smaller than the number of points inside the rectangle. If a rectangle contains thousands of points and one dominates all others, the requested bound permits only $O(\log\log N)$ time beyond outputting that one point. Reporting every point and filtering afterward cannot meet it. The data structure must skip large dominated regions without paying for their contents.

Counting and reporting have different targets. Four-sided skyline counting needs $\Omega(\log N/\log\log N)$ query time at near-linear space. That does not directly refute fast reporting: counting by enumeration costs an additional $k$, which can be large. The known reporting upper bound pays the same logarithmic overhead as counting, plus the output size.

The 2026 paper distinguishes the top-open and bottom-open three-sided variants and explicitly leaves the four-sided reporting bound unresolved. The missing side of a rectangle can change the problem, so results for three-sided queries do not settle this card.
why: This asks whether selecting only undominated answers imposes an inherent indexing cost beyond locating a range and emitting its output. I include it as a focused data-structure problem with a precise model, a concrete gap, and a useful distinction between counting, reporting, and output-sensitive computation.
definitions:
Coordinates are already in rank space; this avoids hiding a separate predecessor-search cost for a larger universe. The set is static. Space is measured in machine words, not bits. The factor $\log^{O(1)}N$ has a fixed exponent. The output parameter $k$ is query-dependent, and no scan of all of $P\cap Q$ is allowed unless its cost fits the stated bound.

The target is deterministic exact reporting with polynomial preprocessing time, using the usual word-RAM operations: arithmetic, multiplication, bitwise Boolean operations, shifts, comparisons, and indirect addressing on a constant number of words.

progress.text: Brodal and Larsen obtain an $O(N)$-word counting structure with $O(\log N/\log\log N)$ query time and a matching cell-probe lower bound. Their reporting tradeoff includes $O(N\log^{\varepsilon}N)$ space and $O(\log N/\log\log N+k)$ query time for fixed $\varepsilon>0$.
Kushwaha and Nekrich ask whether near-linear-space four-sided skyline reporting can attain $O(\log\log N+k)$, the optimal ordinary four-sided range-reporting bound.
